questions.prompt: What does @MainActor actually guarantee, and how is it different from calling DispatchQueue.main.async?

expectedConcepts.text: @MainActor isolates the annotated code to the main actor
It is a compile-time guarantee, checked statically
Calling into it from elsewhere requires await, which hops to the main actor
DispatchQueue.main.async is a runtime scheduling call with no compile-time checking

misconceptions.text: @MainActor makes the call run synchronously on the main thread from any context

modelAnswerOutline: @MainActor marks code as isolated to the main actor.
The compiler then refuses unsafe access from other isolation domains — it is a static guarantee.
From a non-main context you must await, which suspends and resumes on the main actor.
DispatchQueue.main.async only schedules at runtime; nothing verifies you remembered.
Over-annotating whole services with @MainActor to silence warnings serializes work that need not be.
